qs.q: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta&1\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta&3\end{bmatrix}$ be the augmented matrix of a linear system. This system ----
e: The coefficient matrix is $C=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$.
$\det C=\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1\neq 0$ for every $\theta$, so $C$ is invertible.
By the Invertible Matrix Theorem, $CX=b$ has exactly one solution $X=C^{-1}b$ for every $b$ (here $b=(1,3)^T$).
A system that has a solution is consistent, for every value of $\theta$.

qs.q: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-2&1\\-3&6&3\end{bmatrix}$ be the augmented matrix of a linear system. This system has ----
e: Apply $R_2\to R_2+3R_1$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&-2&1\\0&0&6\end{bmatrix}$.
The second row represents the equation $0x+0y=6$, which is impossible.
A row of the form $[0\ 0\ |\ c]$ with $c\neq 0$ means the system is inconsistent, so it has no solution.

qs.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&3&1\\2&7&3\end{bmatrix}$ is the augmented matrix of a linear system, then the system has ----
e: Apply $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&3&1\\0&1&1\end{bmatrix}$.
The matrix is already in row-echelon form: both columns of the coefficient part have a leading 1 and there is no contradictory row.
From row 2: $y=1$. Back-substitute in row 1: $x+3(1)=1\Rightarrow x=-2$.
There is exactly one solution, $(x,y)=(-2,1)$.

qs.q: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\4&2&2\end{bmatrix}$ be the augmented matrix of a linear system. This system has ----
e: Apply $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$: $\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}$.
The zero row means the second equation is redundant (it is just twice the first).
Only one equation remains, $2x+y=1$, for two unknowns, so $y=t$ is a free parameter and $x=\frac{1-t}{2}$.
A consistent system with a free variable has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&3&-4\\-1&-2&2\\3&6&6\end{bmatrix}$ be the augmented matrix of a linear system. This system has ----
e: $R_1\to-\frac12R_1$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&-\frac32&2\\-1&-2&2\\3&6&6\end{bmatrix}$.
$R_2\to R_2+R_1$ and $R_3\to R_3-3R_1$: $\begin{bmatrix}1&-\frac32&2\\0&-\frac72&4\\0&\frac{21}{2}&0\end{bmatrix}$.
Row 2 gives $-\frac72y=4\Rightarrow y=-\frac87$, while row 3 gives $\frac{21}{2}y=0\Rightarrow y=0$.
These two requirements contradict each other, so the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

qs.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&3&b_1\\2&5&b_2\end{bmatrix}$ is the augmented matrix of a linear system and $\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}$ is a solution of it, then $\begin{bmatrix}b_1\\b_2\end{bmatrix}=$ ----
e: The system is $x+3y=b_1$ and $2x+5y=b_2$.
A solution must satisfy both equations: substitute $x=1,\ y=0$.
So $\begin{bmatrix}b_1\\b_2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$.
